title: Bulls on Parade and the marching clubs
summary: He recalls a Black parade organization with a bull on ropes, the origin of his parade tune for Bob Crosby.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: So you heard music around the home, and did you get out, like, at carnival time? Get out what? At carnival time. Around Mardi Gras, anything like that?

Yeah, I'd go listen to different bands there, and that's how I got the South Rampart Street Parade idea in my head. My uncle used to take me, you got the stower there anyway, he used to take me to see. But I used to go see it on Rampart, not on Rampart, on Claiborne and Espinay.
They had this colored organization, used to have, I used to call it the Bulls on Parade. Mm-hmm.

And then, and they were all, all, all marching and having, had a wonderful band, see, all the time. I listened to that band all the time, and Marco, I said, I used to tell Marco, take me over to see the Bulls off Parade. So, all these guys were dressed in full dress suits, you understand? Mm-hmm. I used to call it Swallowtail Coach, you know? Yeah. And they were dressed like, like, like, like guys in a minstrel. And, and for, they, they had that, that, that, that hi-hat and everything else. And they were strutting. Mm-hmm. And that band was playing. They were strutting like that. And they had a, for the bouquet, they had a big cauliflower. And the 10 cents to go stuck right in there. Just like in the minstrel show, you know?
And, and the front of their parade, they had a, a real ferocious looking bull. Mm-hmm. With a rig in his nose. And they had this cord, this rope.

Tied to that rig. And half of it was stretched to one side of the street, the other one to the other side of the street. Now, they got two guys to handle those ropes, see? One and one on each side. Mm-hmm. Now, they're strutting along, and this, this is leading the parade. And the band's come marching, and they're strutting along. Mm-hmm. And these two guys, they weren't worried about looking at the other guy on the other side. And they weren't, we're, we're looking at, at, at the, at the bull itself. But they were worried, if that guy let that rope go on the other side, all hell would break out, you understand? Yeah. So that, that's, that's the story on the thing, see? Mm-hmm. And, and it's all written down in black and white there. I mean, it's a cute story. I tried to form it, the way I saw it and the way I remembered it. And, and I said, one of these days I'm going to write a tune to represent this. It's, it's got to be a parade, it's got to be a parade march. And, and, well, the whole story is that when, when we got together with Haggard and wrote the thing out, see? Mm-hmm. And, uh, it got to, it got to be a pretty famous flag waver for, for the Bob Crosby band. And now all, all bands play every once in a while, you know. Mm-hmm. Sure.
I hear, I hear brass bands played in parades and everything.
Sure. Well, all, all the school bands had, all, all had it also.
